subject: Dedicated capacity: throughput guarantee scoping & measurement methodology
messages:
From: Will Chen <will.chen@acme.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@acme.ai>
Date: 2027-08-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated commit throughput - initial ask

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo week. We're close to a commercial decision but need a clear, measurable throughput guarantee for the Dedicated pool before we sign the SOW. High-level ask: a committed pool that can sustain ~220k tokens/sec for our production mix (mix attached in SOW_draft.pdf) with p95 inference latency <= 150ms for single-turn generation. 

A few clarifying questions for your measurement plan:
- How do you map tokens/sec to requests/sec for chat-style workloads where message length varies?
- Do you include KV cache warm-up in the measurement window?
- What happens to our discount if the verified throughput is lower than the committed figure?

Attached: SOW_draft.pdf (contains expected traffic distribution and peak hour traffic). Can we get a short write-up of the proposed verification methodology so procurement can sign off?

Thanks,
Will Chen
Head of Platform, Acme AI
will.chen@acme.ai

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-18T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit throughput - initial ask

Hi Will — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. Looping in Ben and Karthik for pricing/commit detail. Below is a concise verification approach we recommend; happy to expand into a formal runbook.

Summary (short):
- Measurement target: sustained tokens/sec for the customer-produced mix (not synthetic short-run spikes). We'll report tokens/sec and equivalent requests/sec at the measured distribution.
- Measurement window: 72 continuous hours, with first 6 hours considered warm-up and excluded from final sustained metric.
- Latency metrics: report p50/p95/p99 for inference-only (model inference time) and end-to-end (including network and routing). Acceptance uses p95 end-to-end <= 150ms (per your ask).
- KV cache: run two phases — cold start (to validate model cold performance) and warmed phase (to show steady-state with KV hits). Primary acceptance on warmed steady-state.
- Traffic replay: we prefer a production traffic replay from your captured traces (sanitized). If unavailable, we'll run a synthetic mix matching the SOW distribution (short: 60%, medium: 30%, long: 10%).

Detailed points and rationale:
1) Tokens vs requests: tokens/sec is the strongest measure of throughput for generative workloads because tokenization varies. We will also provide requests/sec for the measured distribution. For chat with function-calls, we count tokens generated by the model (output tokens) plus encoded input tokens for throughput accounting.

2) Measurement harness: we will run our standard throughput harness (attached throughput-harness-spec.md) on your Dedicated pool. Harness details: multi-client replay, configurable think times to mimic user behavior, backpressure handling, and KV cache control. Metrics emitted: tokens/sec (windowed, 1s/10s/60s), request concurrency, model GPU utilization, per-GPU memory stats, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and KV hit rate.

3) Sampling & windows: we report both the sustained 95th-percentile tokens/sec across non-warm windows and the maximum 5-minute rolling sustained tokens/sec seen. Acceptance requires the sustained 95% metric to meet the committed band.

4) Failure modes and credits: if verified sustained throughput is below the committed band by >10% for the acceptance window, we'll offer either a pro-rated usage credit (one-time) or an additional short-term capacity uplift at no charge while we remediate. Exact credit percentages are tied to commit bands — Ben will propose ranges below.

5) Hardware config: please confirm preferred GPU type. Our baseline proposal for your commit level is 16x A100-80GB (mixed-precision, q4/qaquant profiles) with RDMA-enabled networking. If you plan heavier long-context usage, we may recommend more memory-optimized nodes.

Next steps:
- Ben: pricing and credit band proposal (see Ben's note).
- Will: confirm if you can provide a sanitized traffic replay or whether we should synthesize.
- Sofia: we'll schedule the 72-hour acceptance window once SOW and hardware are provisioned.

Attachments: throughput-harness-spec.md (detailed spec).

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Thanks, Sofia — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) Tokens definition: for our billing/observability we often use "generated tokens only" vs "input+output". Which do you report for the throughput SLA?

2) Quantization/precision: our models will use int8 q4 variants in production. Will the acceptance run use our production quantization? If not, how do we ensure parity?

3) Function calls: in some flows the model returns structured function args (short outputs) but triggers a follow-up system request. Should those downstream system latencies be part of the end-to-end SLA or excluded?

We can provide a sanitized 7-day capture for a replay — I'll confirm with procurement. Also, we'll need the exact measurement start/stop protocol so our infra team can schedule maintenance windows.

On credits: we prefer a clear mapping (underperform -> percent credit) rather than case-by-case.

--
Will

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Will Chen <will.chen@acme.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-19T10:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated commit throughput - initial ask (pricing & credits)

Hi Will,

Short version on pricing/credits: we map commit bands to discount tiers and to a simple credit schedule for measurement shortfalls. Proposed bands (starting point):
- Band A: >= 200k sustained tokens/sec => 30% on-host discount; shortfall credit = 10% of monthly commit value if verified throughput < band by >10%
- Band B: 125k-200k => 20% discount; shortfall credit = 6%
- Band C: 60k-125k => 10% discount; shortfall credit = 3%

If verification shows shortfall but within 10%, we offer operational remediation and a one-time usage credit equivalent to 50% of the difference prorated for the first billing month. If shortfall >10% we automatically apply the credit above OR offer a complimentary capacity uplift until remediation completes (your choice).

On measurement parity: acceptance runs will use the quantization profile you plan to ship in production. If you need a separate run for a different quantization profile, we can do that at no charge once per commit.

Finally, if you choose a longer commit (12+ months) we can deepen the discount bands by 5 percentage points and widen the remediation window (we'll propose an SLA playbook).

Happy to put exact dollar math into the SOW; attaching a simple pricing-tiers.xlsx for transparency.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Will — thanks for the quick replies and for confirming you'll check on the 7-day capture. Final operational checklist so procurement can sign the SOW: 

1) Measurement: 72-hour acceptance window, first 6 hours warm-up, report sustained 95% tokens/sec over remaining window. We will run with your production quantization (int8/q4) and the replay you provide.

2) Acceptance criteria: sustained 220k tokens/sec (per SOW) during steady-state + p95 end-to-end latency <= 150ms. If you opt for the Band A commit we discussed, pricing/credits map applies.

3) Scheduling: we propose the acceptance window start on 2027-08-31 00:00 UTC (provisioning permitting). Please confirm any blackout windows by 2027-08-24.

4) Signing: I'll kick off DocuSign once you confirm the replay availability and blackout windows. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF123456

5) Post-acceptance: We'll provide a runbook with the raw harness logs and a performance dashboard. Any remediation timeline will be mutually agreed in the SOW appendix.

If procurement prefers the automatic credit schedule instead of remediation-first, we can reflect that option in the SOW as an explicit checkbox.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
